title: Upside compensation ratio: are you paid enough for the upside you sell?
summary: When you sell a covered call or cash-secured put, you sell your upside for income today. If the upside you give up is worth $10 and you collect $1, you are not paid enough; if you collect about $7, the trade looks good. The speaker calls this comparison the upside compensation ratio.

steps.caption: The stock trades at $100. We sell a call against 100 shares.
The dashed lines: long stock and the short call.
The covered call payoff: income today, upside capped at the strike.
The upside you give away is the area above the strike. Value it before you sell it.
The premium is your pay. $1 for $10 of upside is too little; $7 sounds fair.
Breakeven is the stock price minus the premium.

takeaways: Selling a covered call or a put means selling your upside for current income.
Compare the premium with the value of the upside you give up.
The speaker calls this ratio the upside compensation ratio.
caveats: The metric's formula is not given in the clip and is not verified.
The waitlist and website mentions are promotional.
